_meta.note: Structural regression golden. main-de-truncation-guard: the 12-section schema truncated at max_tokens 4000 in German → fixed with max_tokens 6000 + caps (response_strategies 3-4, what_NOT_to_say 3-4). 10 annotations stripped (glued onto response_text/tactic fields). PF-26 fixed. manipulation_tactics + draft_analysis.tone_flags/problematic_phrases neutralized to [] (interpretation-dependent). Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v2): adopted PF-39 v2 WITH an enforcement profile (router.outputGuard), and the schema lost everything the guard forbids — emotional_temperature, primary_emotion_detected, underlying_need, communication_style, the whole manipulation_tactics array, and draft_analysis.escalation_risk.level. A guard that fights its own schema on every call is not enforcement, it is a repair loop. message_analysis is now triggers_identified (quoted phrases only) plus whats_being_asked. cooling_recommendation.delay_time is words, not minutes. The follow-up endpoint no longer passes temperature/emotion/tactics as context. Guard verified firing live: 3 fields flagged and repaired on the first real input (predicted_recipient_reaction, emotion_inference_as_fact, unsupported_timing_rule). Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v3): second schema pass. what_this_does and risks removed from every strategy (an effect and a risk are both predictions about a stranger), and apology_assessment, what_NOT_to_say, timing_landmines, channel_landmines, if_they_continue_escalating and repair_strategy_later deleted whole — they were where the remaining mind-reading and unsupported prescriptions lived. Output is now a grounded read, 3-4 ready-to-send responses, and the follow-up Q&A. triggers_identified may carry a note about the WORDS as a possibility, never a determination about the sender. Both inline copy buttons removed. Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v4): the guard was checking every field EXCEPT the replies — the wiring named response_strategies[i].message and the schema field is response_text, so getByPath returned undefined and every reply was filtered out before the check ran. Also added contradicted_supplied_fact to the V2 checks: told the relationship was Partner, the output called them a roommate, which is a swap rather than an invention and nothing was looking for it. Prompt now pins the supplied relationship word and requires replies to reflect what was SAID, never what is FELT. Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v5): the repair pass was told it could return an empty string rather than filler, and did — a promised response option came back as "". outputGuard now takes requiredNonEmpty and restores the pre-repair value for any deliverable the repair hollowed out; a flawed reply the visitor can edit beats an empty box. Guard terms added: interpretation_as_fact, invented_relationship_dynamic, attitude_label. Check 4 now names attitude verdicts (contempt, disdain, dismissiveness, passive aggression) and "likely meaning" explicitly. Strategy labels must describe the reply, not what it avoids — "holds space without chasing" invented a chasing dynamic. Also a shape guard: response_strategies came back once as a STRING of Python-style pseudo-JSON, which the frontend maps over. Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v6): the prompt was replaced wholesale, and the output is now two keys — message_read and strategies[4]{title,tone,response_text}. goal_reality_check, draft_analysis, cooling_recommendation and message_analysis are gone; the two-call read/respond split went with them, since there is one small schema now. The guard collapsed to four tests: is it addressed to the other person, is it sendable as written, does it pursue the selected goal, does it avoid unsupported facts. Titles are checked as well as replies — "redirect without chasing" invents a dynamic and is the visitor-facing label. Follow-up Coaching and Adjust Tone remain as UI functionality against their own endpoints, not as generated analysis.

input.receivedMessage: You never listen to me. After everything I have done for you, you cannot even show up on time. I guess I am just not important to you.
input.userDraft: Wow you are being so dramatic right now, I was literally 10 minutes late
input.actualGoal: I want them to understand I care but also stop the guilt trips

output.message_read: Three distinct claims load this message: 'you never listen,' 'after everything I have done for you,' and 'I am just not important to you.' The first and third frame the lateness as evidence of a pattern and a feeling of low priority. The middle phrase — 'after everything I have done' — introduces a debt framing that goes beyond this incident. Whether 'never' and 'just not important' reflect a genuine ongoing concern or are heat-of-the-moment intensifiers is ambiguous from the message alone. Any response that only addresses the ten minutes will leave the bigger claims unanswered.

strategies.title: Acknowledge the feeling, name the pattern you want to change
strategies.response_text: I can hear that you felt like I wasn't prioritizing you, and I don't want you to feel that way. I also want to be honest: when it comes out as 'you never' and 'I'm just not important to you,' it's hard for me to hear what you actually need. Can we talk about what's going on? I'd rather understand what you're feeling than have this stay as it is.

strategies.title: Stay brief, open the door without defending
strategies.response_text: I hear you, and I don't want you feeling unimportant to me. I'm not going to argue about the ten minutes. What I do want to do is actually talk, because it sounds like this matters more than just today. When you're ready, I'm here for that conversation.

strategies.title: Name the guilt-trip dynamic gently but clearly
strategies.response_text: I care about you, and I'm sorry I was late. I want to own that. But I have to be honest — 'after everything I've done for you' makes it harder for me to actually hear what you need right now. If being on time matters to you, tell me that directly and I'll take it seriously. I'm open to talking about this.

strategies.title: Redirect toward what you both actually want
strategies.response_text: You matter to me — a lot. Being ten minutes late wasn't a statement about how much I value you. I'm hearing that something about how I'm showing up has bothered you, and I want to understand it. What I can't do is respond well when it comes at me as 'you never' and 'I'm not important to you.' Let's set this specific moment aside and talk about what's really going on. I'm in.

input.receivedMessage: Du hörst mir nie zu. Nach allem, was ich für dich getan habe, kannst du nicht einmal pünktlich sein. Ich schätze, ich bin dir einfach nicht wichtig.
input.userDraft: Wow, du bist gerade so dramatisch, ich war buchstäblich 10 Minuten zu spät
input.actualGoal: Ich möchte, dass sie verstehen, dass ich mich sorge, aber auch die Schuldgefühle stoppen

output.message_read: Drei Aussagen prägen diese Nachricht: 'Du hörst mir nie zu' (eine Verallgemeinerung, die über die Verspätung hinausgeht), 'nach allem, was ich für dich getan habe' (ein Verweis auf frühere Leistungen, der nicht näher benannt wird) und 'ich bin dir einfach nicht wichtig' (eine Aussage über deine Gefühle für sie). Die Verspätung ist der Anlass der Nachricht.

strategies.title: Anerkennen ohne zuzustimmen
strategies.response_text: Ich sehe, dass du frustriert bist, und das nehme ich ernst. Ich war zehn Minuten zu spät — das habe ich verstanden. Mir ist wichtig, dass ich dir nicht gleichgültig bin. Kannst du mir sagen, was dich in dieser Situation beschäftigt?

strategies.title: Eigene Wahrnehmung benennen, Tür offenhalten
strategies.response_text: Ich möchte nicht streiten, und ich möchte auch nicht, dass du glaubst, du bist mir egal — das stimmt nicht. Gleichzeitig tut es mir weh, wenn ich höre, dass ich 'nie' zuhöre. Das möchte ich mit dir klären. Wenn du bereit bist, rede ich gern mit dir.

strategies.title: Kurz und klar, ohne Gegenangriff
strategies.response_text: Ich war heute zu spät, das stimmt, und es tut mir leid. Aber 'du bist mir nicht wichtig' — das ist nicht wahr, und ich möchte nicht, dass das so stehen bleibt. Ich bin da. Sag mir, was du brauchst.

strategies.title: Raum lassen, eigene Grenze benennen
strategies.response_text: Ich sehe, dass du wütend bist. Das nehme ich ernst und ich möchte das mit dir klären — aber ich brauche dazu ein echtes Gespräch. Wenn wir beide etwas ruhiger sind, können wir reden. Ich bin dabei.
